datasets.label: Europe
datasets.sub: From the Magna Carta to the Cold War

events.title: Magna Carta Signed
events.description: King John seals the Great Charter at Runnymede, establishing that the monarch is subject to the rule of law.

events.title: Black Death Reaches Europe
events.description: The bubonic plague arrives in Sicily from Crimea. Over the next five years it kills one-third of Europe's entire population.

events.title: Gutenberg Prints Bible
events.description: Johannes Gutenberg completes the first major book printed in Europe using movable type, revolutionising the spread of knowledge.

events.title: French Revolution
events.description: The storming of the Bastille ignites a radical transformation of France, sweeping away centuries of monarchy and launching the ideals of liberty and equality.

events.title: Napoleon Defeated at Waterloo
events.description: Wellington and Blücher's forces defeat Napoleon at Waterloo, ending the Napoleonic Wars and reshaping Europe's borders.

events.title: Darwin Publishes Origin of Species
events.description: Darwin's theory of evolution by natural selection transforms biology and our understanding of life on Earth.

events.title: First World War Begins
events.description: Austria-Hungary declares war on Serbia following the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, igniting a conflict that kills 20 million people.

events.title: Russian Revolution
events.description: The Bolsheviks seize power in Petrograd, overthrowing the Provisional Government and establishing Soviet rule.

events.title: D-Day Normandy Landings
events.description: Allied forces launch the largest seaborne invasion in history on the beaches of Normandy, turning the tide of World War II.

events.title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
events.description: East Germany opens its borders after 28 years. Jubilant crowds tear down the Wall, ending the Cold War's most potent symbol.

events.title: World Wide Web Invented
events.description: Tim Berners-Lee makes the World Wide Web publicly available at CERN, beginning the transformation of human communication.

events.title: End of Apartheid
events.description: South Africa holds its first fully democratic elections. Nelson Mandela becomes president, ending decades of institutionalised racial segregation.

datasets.label: Americas
datasets.sub: From Columbus to the smartphone era

events.title: Columbus Reaches Americas
events.description: Christopher Columbus makes landfall in the Bahamas, beginning sustained contact between the Old World and the New.

events.title: Declaration of Independence
events.description: The thirteen American colonies declare independence from Britain. Thomas Jefferson's document becomes a foundation of modern democratic thought.

events.title: Louisiana Purchase
events.description: The United States purchases 828,000 square miles from France, doubling the country's size and opening the West.

events.title: American Civil War Begins
events.description: Confederate forces attack Fort Sumter, beginning four years of war that would determine the nation's future and end slavery.

events.title: Wright Brothers First Flight
events.description: Orville Wright pilots the first powered airplane at Kitty Hawk. The flight lasts 12 seconds and covers 37 metres.

events.title: Panama Canal Opens
events.description: The Panama Canal opens, connecting the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans and revolutionising global trade routes.

events.title: Wall Street Crash
events.description: Black Thursday triggers the Great Depression, wiping out millions of investors and plunging the world into economic crisis.

events.title: Moon Landing
events.description: Apollo 11 touches down on the Sea of Tranquility. Neil Armstrong becomes the first human to walk on the Moon.

events.title: Watergate Scandal
events.description: The arrest of five men breaking into the Democratic National Committee HQ begins a political crisis that forces Nixon to resign.

events.title: 9/11 Attacks
events.description: Coordinated terrorist attacks destroy the Twin Towers and hit the Pentagon, killing nearly 3,000 people and reshaping global geopolitics.

events.title: First iPhone Unveiled
events.description: Steve Jobs introduces an iPod, a phone, and an internet communicator in one device. The smartphone era begins.

events.title: Obama Elected President
events.description: Barack Obama becomes the first African-American President of the United States, winning by a decisive electoral margin.

datasets.label: Asia
datasets.sub: From the Mongols to modern geopolitics

events.title: Mongol Empire Founded
events.description: Genghis Khan unites the Mongol tribes and establishes the empire that would become the largest contiguous land empire in history.

events.title: Zheng He's First Voyage
events.description: Chinese admiral Zheng He sets sail with 300 ships and 28,000 men, reaching Southeast Asia, India, Arabia and East Africa.

events.title: Battle of Plassey
events.description: The British East India Company defeats the Nawab of Bengal, beginning British dominance over the Indian subcontinent.

events.title: Meiji Restoration
events.description: Emperor Meiji is restored to power in Japan, beginning rapid modernisation and the transformation of a feudal state into an industrial power.

events.title: Opium War Ends
events.description: China signs the Treaty of Nanking, ceding Hong Kong to Britain and opening treaty ports — the beginning of the 'century of humiliation'.

events.title: Indian Independence
events.description: India gains independence from Britain. The subcontinent is partitioned into India and Pakistan in one of history's largest migrations.

events.title: People's Republic of China Founded
events.description: Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic of China in Tiananmen Square after the Communist Party's victory in the civil war.

events.title: Korean War Armistice
events.description: An armistice ends active fighting in the Korean War, leaving the peninsula divided at the 38th parallel — a division that persists today.

events.title: Vietnam War Ends
events.description: North Vietnamese forces capture Saigon, ending 20 years of war and reunifying Vietnam under communist rule.

events.title: Tiananmen Square Protests
events.description: The Chinese military crushes pro-democracy protests in Tiananmen Square, killing hundreds in an event still censored in China.

events.title: Sputnik Launched
events.description: The Soviet Union launches the first artificial Earth satellite, triggering the Space Race and shocking the Western world.

events.title: Atomic Bomb on Hiroshima
events.description: The United States drops an atomic bomb on Hiroshima, Japan, killing 80,000 instantly and ushering in the nuclear age.
